summary: A rubblestone tower at the mouth of Sippican Harbor, lit in 1819, discontinued in 1933, relit as a solar light in 1997.

structures.note: Tower shape conical per the NRHP form and USLHS; height recorded as 25 ft (NRHP), 29 ft (LHF), 31 ft base to lantern centre (USLHS)
Stone dwelling attached to the tower (NRHP); demolished by 1890 (LHF)
Frame house on the old foundation (LHF). USLHS records the 1890 keeper's quarters as stone
Bell tower with a fog bell struck by machinery (LHF only)

access.note: Tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Island off-limits mid-May to mid-August, the tern nesting season (LighthouseFriends). USLHS record: 'Open to Public: No'. Owner: Town of Marion. Check the current position with the Town before publishing.

events.note: Tower constructed, attached to a stone dwelling (NRHP chronology). The NRHP significance statement says 1817
Activated 1 September 1819 (LHF); USLHS gives 1819 as the year established
Fourth-order Fresnel per LHF and USLHS. The Board's 1899 report describes a fifth-order light in 1898
New lantern room (LHF)
Sea swept over the island in November, filling the well and cellar and damaging the seawall (LHF)
Storm of 8 September 1869 carried away outbuildings and destroyed 280 feet of seawall (LHF)
Frame dwelling built on the old foundation (LHF). USLHS records stone quarters, 1890
About 150 feet of close board fence rebuilt (Board report)
Old lantern and deck replaced (Board report)
Boat-house enlarged and rebuilt, 286 running feet of fence built (Board report)
Bell tower and 1,000-pound fog bell struck by machinery (LHF only)
Keeper Maurice A. Babcock rescued a young man from a small boat that capsized near the station, 12 September
Keeper George T. Gustavus towed a disabled motorboat into Marion Harbor, 29 March
Light discontinued; lighted buoys took over its work (LHF). USLHS: discontinued 1933
Hurricane washed away the outbuildings (NRHP); the storm surge destroyed all other structures on the island (LHF)
NRHP: sold to town after being declared surplus. Conflicts with LHF, which has a 1940 auction, a sale to Augustus Fiske and the town buying from his heirs in 1966
Town of Marion bought the island from Augustus Fiske's heirs for $2,500 (LHF)
Restored by town and Sippican Historical Society with local contributions of $13,000; automatic beacon installed; relit briefly (NRHP, LHF)
Tower vandalized, then restored again by the Historical Society (NRHP)
Bird Island Preservation Society formed to restore the lighthouse (LHF)
Relit 4 July 1997 with a solar-powered automatic light (LHF)
Corps of Engineers revetment of about 1,100 feet, construction from December 2015; article of June 2017 (USACE)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 'Sources differ on whether the light is still lit': it was discontinued in 1933 (USLHS, LHF), relit 4 July 1997 as a solar light (LHF), and listed as an active aid to navigation (USLHS 'Active Aid to Navigation: Yes'). The 2017 USACE article calls it a still-operating light. Status 'active' stands.

notes_for_editor: 1) Dates disagree: the NRHP significance statement says 'Constructed in 1817' against 1819 in its own chronology, LHF and USLHS. 2) Lens order: LHF and USLHS give a fourth-order Fresnel in 1856; the Board's report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1899 mentions a lens-lantern light 'shown in place of fifth-order light' from 28 to 30 September 1898. Not settled. 3) The 1890 keepers' dwelling: LHF says frame, USLHS says stone. 4) Sale history: NRHP 1939 sale to town vs LHF 1940 auction, Fiske, town purchase in 1966. Both are footnoted. 5) LHF-only claims (not confirmed in a primary source here, because the corpus Lighthouse Board volumes start in 1891): the 1842 Clark letter, the Murray family story, the 1869 storm details, the 1902 bell tower, the 1940 auction, Babcock's 1923 rescue details beyond the Bulletin. 6) The LHF legends about William S. Moore are not repeated; LHF calls one of them 'a popular, but unsubstantiated story', and the story says only that. 7) The USLHS roster lists one 'Contractor', Bela Pratt, with no dates; he is not a keeper and is left out. 8) Bird Island in Galveston Bar (Texas), 'Bird Island Flats' (LSS tables) and the Boston Bay Bird Island beacon in the 1893 Board report are other places and are not used. 9) Chronicling America searches for Bird Island and Sippican returned HTTP 520 errors from loc.gov and no usable hits. 10) The NRHP form is OCR text; some letter-spaced lines were avoided and the clean copy was used for quotes. 11) The LHF date for the Corps project (2016, $3.1 million) differs from the USACE article (construction began December 2015; total project $5.1 million; construction contract $3.6 million). The story gives the USACE date and notes LHF's 2016. The USACE article also calls the light 'still-operating'; the story does not repeat that. 12) Visiting status is from LHF (2026 season not checked) and the USLHS record ('Open to Public: No'). The access level is 'closed' because no source says the island is open outside the nesting season. Recheck with the Town of Marion before publishing. 13) 'Reached only by boat' is not in any source; the story says the island lies offshore and LHF says the light is best viewed from a boat. 14) Matched by position or read from OCR and checked against the page image or the printed page: the Board volume scan pages (238, 29, 90, 60) were confirmed with corpus.py page; the Bulletin PDF pages (1923 p.40, 1930 p.20) were confirmed the same way. The Board volume title-page fiscal years are read from OCR ('FISCAL TEAR EI^DED JU^E 30, 1895', 'FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 80, 1899'). The 1930 rescue date ('on M~rch 29') is OCR from the Bulletin; LHF gives only 'March 1930'; the page image was not viewed. 15) No photos added.
